subject: physical-education
title: Performance task build: dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect under transfer
focus: dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect
essentialQuestion: What can movement say that words cannot?
privacySafeScenario: Compose, refine, and perform a short original movement sequence for an audience of one trusted adult, or describe and notate it in full if the learner prefers not to perform.
studentTask: Learner works dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect carried through a complete sequence run without stopping, where a lost count is recovered mid-phrase instead of restarting at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect carried through a complete sequence run without stopping, where a lost count is recovered mid-phrase instead of restarting, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where dance forms across cultures, treated with accuracy and respect shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
